subject: Physics
prompt: Work done by normal force on a body moving on a horizontal surface is?
explain: Normal force ⊥ displacement on horizontal surface → W = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: A variable force F(x) does work from x₁ to x₂ given by?
explain: Work by variable force is the integral of F(x) over displacement.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work-energy theorem for a system of particles involves?
explain: Work-energy theorem: net work done on a system equals change in its kinetic energy.

subject: Physics
prompt: Kilowatt-hour (kWh) is a unit of?
explain: kWh is a commercial unit of energy; 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

subject: Physics
prompt: 1 horsepower (hp) equals how many watts?
explain: 1 horsepower = 746 W (metric: 735.5 W; British: 746 W used in JEE).

subject: Physics
prompt: A force F = kx² is conservative because?
explain: A force is conservative if work done between two points is path-independent.

subject: Physics
prompt: Pseudo work done by pseudo force on a body in non-inertial frame is?
explain: Pseudo forces do real work in non-inertial frames and must be included in work-energy theorem.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work done by tension on a body moving in a vertical circle at the top?
explain: Tension is centripetal (radial), always perpendicular to velocity, so work = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: A body is projected vertically up. At maximum height, its mechanical energy is?
explain: Mechanical energy is conserved; at top, all KE converts to PE = mgh_max = initial KE.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work done by internal forces in a rigid body is?
explain: In a rigid body, relative displacements between particles are zero, so internal work = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: Unit of spring constant k in SI system is?
explain: k = F/x → N/m is the SI unit of spring constant.

subject: Physics
prompt: Potential energy of a system of two charges is a form of?
explain: Electrostatic force is conservative; associated PE is conservative PE.

subject: Physics
prompt: A body moves up a frictionless incline. Work done by normal reaction is?
explain: Normal reaction is always perpendicular to displacement, so it does zero work.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work done by friction depends on?
explain: Friction is non-conservative; work done depends on path length, not endpoints.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work done by a force on a body moving along a closed frictionless loop is?
explain: For conservative forces, work done over any closed path is zero.

subject: Physics
prompt: When a rubber ball hits a wall and bounces back with same speed, the collision is?
explain: Same speed before and after → e = 1 → perfectly elastic collision.

subject: Physics
prompt: An engine develops power P. Time to do work W is?
explain: Power P = W/t, so t = W/P; time is inversely proportional to power.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a body in neutral equilibrium on a PE curve, d²U/dx² is?
explain: Neutral equilibrium: dU/dx = 0 and d²U/dx² = 0; PE is constant in that region.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work done by all external forces on a system of particles equals change in?
explain: Work-energy theorem for a system: W_ext = ΔKE_total (treating particles independently).

subject: Physics
prompt: A force does positive work on a body. The speed of the body?
explain: Positive work → positive ΔKE → increase in speed by work-energy theorem.

subject: Physics
prompt: A body slides up a rough incline. Work done by friction is?
explain: Friction opposes motion (up incline), so it acts downward along incline; W_friction < 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work done by applied force on a body moving at constant velocity on rough surface?
explain: Applied force equals friction magnitude; displacement is along force, so work is positive.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work done by a variable force F = 3x N from x=0 to x=4 m is?

subject: Physics
prompt: A block moves on a frictionless surface. Work done by gravity is?
explain: On a horizontal frictionless surface, gravity is perpendicular to displacement; W = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: Efficiency of a machine is defined as?
explain: Efficiency η = useful output power / total input power (dimensionless, ≤1).

subject: Physics
prompt: The work done by a force in moving a body along a frictionless curved path depends on?
explain: For a conservative force, work depends only on initial and final positions, not path.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work done by tension in a string on a simple pendulum over one complete oscillation is?
explain: Tension is always perpendicular to motion of bob; net work over full cycle is zero.

subject: Physics
prompt: When a light mass m₁ hits a very heavy stationary mass m₂ elastically, m₁ rebounds with?
explain: For m₁ << m₂, v₁' ≈ -u₁; light body bounces back with nearly same speed.

subject: Physics
prompt: A particle moves under a force F = -kx. The PE of this system is?
explain: F = -dU/dx = -kx gives U = ½kx² (choosing U=0 at x=0).

subject: Physics
prompt: The work done by air resistance on a projectile over its entire trajectory is?
explain: Air resistance always opposes velocity; work by it is always negative (non-conservative).

subject: Physics
prompt: For a spring-block system, total mechanical energy at any point is?
explain: Total ME = KE + PE = ½mv² + ½kx² = constant (no friction).

subject: Physics
prompt: The energy released when two protons (same charge) are brought closer is?
explain: Like charges repel; PE increases as they approach; energy must be supplied (absorbed), not released.

subject: Physics
prompt: A person carrying a load walks horizontally on flat ground. Work done by him against gravity is?
explain: Gravity acts vertically; horizontal displacement ⊥ gravity; W_gravity = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: Slope of KE vs. x (displacement) graph for a constant force gives?
explain: By work-energy theorem, dW = F dx = dKE; so slope dKE/dx = F.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two bodies have same momentum. Body with greater mass has ___ KE.
explain: KE = p²/2m; for same p, greater m gives lesser KE.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work done by a force F on a body is negative when angle θ between F and d satisfies?
explain: cosθ < 0 when 90° < θ < 270°, making W = Fd cosθ negative.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work done by a force F along displacement d at angle θ is?
explain: Only the component of force along displacement does work; W = Fd cosθ.

subject: Physics
prompt: A body of mass m moves up height h on a rough incline. Loss in ME equals?
explain: Only non-conservative forces (friction) cause loss in mechanical energy; ΔME = W_friction.

subject: Physics
prompt: A spring of constant k is cut into n equal parts. Spring constant of each part?
explain: Shorter spring has higher stiffness; each part has spring constant nk.

subject: Physics
prompt: In a head-on elastic collision, velocity of lighter mass m₁ hitting heavier m₂ at rest?
explain: When m₁ < m₂, (m₁−m₂) < 0, so m₁ rebounds in opposite direction.

subject: Physics
prompt: If a body is pulled up a frictionless incline at constant speed, net work done on it is?
explain: Constant speed means ΔKE = 0; by work-energy theorem, net work = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a body sliding down a rough incline of height h, speed at bottom satisfies?
explain: Friction removes energy; KE gained = mgh − |W_friction|, so v < √(2gh).

subject: Physics
prompt: Ratio of KE lost to initial KE in perfectly inelastic collision of equal masses?
explain: Initial KE = ½mv²; final KE = ¼mv²; loss = ¼mv²; ratio = (¼mv²)/(½mv²) = 1/2.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work done by a force when displacement is zero is?
explain: W = F·d·cosθ; if d = 0, work done is zero regardless of force.

subject: Physics
prompt: A body of mass m is thrown vertically up with speed u. Work done by gravity till it returns?
explain: Gravity is conservative; net displacement is zero on return, so total work = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: Energy stored in a spring when stretched by x₁ then further by x₂ (total extension x₁+x₂)?
explain: PE depends only on total deformation from natural length; U = ½k(x₁+x₂)².

subject: Physics
prompt: A ball of mass m falls from height h onto a spring of constant k. Maximum compression x satisfies?
explain: Ball falls h then compresses spring by x; total PE lost = mg(h+x) = spring PE = ½kx².

subject: Physics
prompt: If a body's KE is K and mass is m, its speed v is?
explain: From K = ½mv², solving gives v = √(2K/m).

subject: Physics
prompt: A block of mass m on frictionless surface hits spring k, compresses by x. Block's initial speed?
explain: Energy conservation: ½mv² = ½kx², gives v = x√(k/m).

subject: Physics
prompt: For a body, if force and displacement are in same direction, work done is?
explain: When θ = 0°, cosθ = 1; W = Fd > 0, so work done is positive.

subject: Physics
prompt: Power–velocity graph for a body under constant force F is?
explain: P = Fv; for constant F, P is linearly proportional to v — straight line through origin.

subject: Physics
prompt: Work done by tension in lifting a mass m by rope through height h at constant speed?
explain: At constant speed, tension = mg; W_T = mgh (positive, upward displacement).

subject: Physics
prompt: A body moves on a frictionless surface. Which force does zero work always?
explain: Normal force is always perpendicular to displacement on a horizontal surface; W = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: In elastic collision between equal masses where one is at rest, KE transferred is?
explain: Equal masses in elastic collision exchange velocities; first stops, second moves with initial speed — 100% KE transfer.

subject: Physics
prompt: A body of mass m falls from h, bounces elastically off floor. Total work by gravity in one round trip is?
explain: Gravity is conservative; net displacement over a closed path is zero, so net work done by gravity is zero.
